fact: Zambia Police Service spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi said creating and spreading false, manipulated or misleading content through computer systems, which he applied to AI-generated content, is an offence under the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025.

The Zambia Cyber Security Agency said creating, altering or sharing misleading AI-generated audio, video and images may be an offence under Section 19 of the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025, with a fine up to K280,000 and 2 to 7 years in prison.

Zambia Police spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi said a 19-year-old was detained in an identity theft and impersonation case over a suspected AI-generated image of a musician in an army uniform, reported on 6 October 2026.

Lusaka Times reports ZICTA director general Collins Mbulo saying on 16 February 2026 that the Cyber Security Act of 2025 will be strictly enforced against people who misuse social media and AI to create fake images and videos of the President and others.

ZICTA's director general said that, working with other law enforcement agencies, it had apprehended some internet abusers, many now appearing before the courts, in the context of AI-generated fake images and videos of the President; no case is named.
